title: Commonwealth Fusion Systems nükleer reaktör için dev tedarik anlaşması imzaladı
summary: Bill Gates destekli Commonwealth Fusion Systems, ticari nükleer füzyon reaktörleri inşa etmek için Fujikura ile rekor düzeyde süperiletken bant anlaşması yaptı.
body:
Bill Gates destekli nükleer füzyon şirketi Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS), Japon üretici Fujikura Ltd. ile ticari füzyon reaktörleri için dev bir tedarik anlaşması imzaladı. Interesting Engineering'in aktardığına göre bu anlaşma, sektörün küçük ölçekli laboratuvar testlerinden endüstriyel üretime geçişinde kritik bir adım olarak öne çıkıyor.

## Süperiletken bantlar ve manyetik alanlar

CFS, ilk ticari füzyon santrali filosunu inşa etmek amacıyla 10 bin kilometreden fazla yüksek sıcaklıkta süperiletken bant satın alacak. Şirketin tasarımı, yıldız koşullarını taklit eden halka şeklindeki tokamak odalarına dayanıyor. 100 milyon dereceden sıcak plazmayı kontrol etmek için gereken güçlü mıknatıslar, bu özel bantlar sayesinde daha küçük alanlarda üretilebilecek ve maliyetleri düşürecek.

İlk bant teslimatları, dünyanın ilk şebeke ölçeğindeki füzyon tesisi olması planlanan Fall Line Fusion Power Station'ın hazırlıklarının yapıldığı Virginia eyaletindeki Chesterfield County'ye gönderilecek. Şirket yöneticisi Bob Mumgaard, bu ortaklığın ARC enerji santralini hayata geçirme hazırlıklarının bir parçası olduğunu belirtti. Öte yandan CFS, Güney Koreli Hyundai Motor Group'un da katılımıyla 1 milyar dolar yeni sermaye yatırımı almıştı.

**Neden önemli?** Japonya ve ABD arasında gelişmiş imalat alanındaki bağları güçlendiren bu anlaşma, ticari füzyon santrallerinin 2030'lu yıllarda bölge şebekelerine elektrik sağlamasını hedefleyen süreci hızlandırıyor.

source_texts.title: Bill Gates-backed nuclear fusion firm inks record 6,200-mile reactor tape deal for grids
source_texts.summary: Commercial nuclear fusion has moved one step closer to reality. Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS) has...
source_texts.text:
Commercial nuclear fusion has moved one step closer to reality. Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS) has signed the largest supply deal of its kind with Japanese manufacturer Fujikura Ltd.
Under the agreement, CFS will purchase more than 10,000 kilometers (around 6215 miles) of high-temperature superconducting (HTS) tape to build its first fleet of commercial power stations.
Fujikura is expanding its production lines in Japan. The agreement signals a critical shift for the fusion industry. Teams are moving past small-scale lab tests and assembling the industrial supply chain needed to build actual power stations.
The first tape deliveries will head to Chesterfield County, Virginia. There, CFS is preparing its flagship Fall Line Fusion Power Station, designed to be the world’s first grid-scale fusion facility.
Keeping the energy contained
CFS’s design centers around a tokamak, which is a hollow, ring-shaped chamber designed to recreate the conditions of a star. Inside the tokamak, extreme heat and pressure force atomic nuclei together.
The challenge is keeping that reaction contained. The resulting plasma reaches temperatures of over 100 million degrees, far hotter than the center of the sun, and would vaporize any physical wall it touches. Only invisible, highly concentrated magnetic fields can suspend it safely in place.
This engineering hurdle explains why the Fujikura contract is so pivotal. Early fusion reactors relied on bulky, low-temperature magnets that generated modest magnetic fields and demanded sprawling cooling systems. To generate sufficient power, those experimental facilities had to be built on an enormous scale.
Building stronger electromagnets
HTS tape allows engineers to build stronger electromagnets within a compact footprint. These intense magnetic fields trap high-energy plasma inside a far smaller vessel, dramatically reducing construction costs and engineering complexity.
CFS is currently constructing SPARC, a prototype machine designed to prove net energy gain—meaning the reaction produces more power than it consumes. Once SPARC hits that milestone, the company plans to replicate the design at commercial scale under the plant name ARC.
“This partnership with Fujikura demonstrates how we’re actively placing orders and getting ready to execute our ARC power plant,” said Bob Mumgaard, chief executive of CFS. He noted that scaling the technology requires global partners willing to invest ahead of commercial deployment.
Global funding support
The move also tightens trade ties between Tokyo and Washington in advanced manufacturing. Fujikura chief executive Naoki Okada said the deal will establish a long-term business base extending into the 2030s, when commercial fusion plants are expected to feed electricity into regional grids.
The announcement caps a busy funding period for CFS. Backed by Bill Gates, the American developer recently raised $1bn in fresh capital. That round included direct investment from South Korea’s Hyundai Motor Group to explore manufacturing partnerships.
With money in hand and key components secured, the company is betting that private industry can deliver clean fusion energy ahead of state-run initiatives.
